title: The Inner Work of Building Wealth
subtitle: The IntentField Wealth Primer
status: Opening chapter and workbook sample · September 2026
opening: Maya closes the laptop, then opens it again. The proposal is finished. She has checked the numbers three times. There is nothing left to prepare, but she cannot bring herself to press send.

She is thirty-nine. She knows her work is good. People recommend her, thank her, and come back. Yet the moment she puts a price on that work, something changes. She begins imagining the client's reaction. Too expensive. Too ambitious. Who does she think she is?

So she lowers the price. For a moment, she feels relief. By the next morning, the relief has become frustration. Another project that will take too much of her time for too little return. Another promise to do it differently next time.

Jordan is twenty-four and has a different version of the same moment. He has saved tutorials about editing videos, building an AI service, and opening an online store. Each new possibility feels like a fresh start. His first offer is still a draft.

Your version may look different again. Perhaps you want your own place, a business that belongs to you, a beautiful trip, or more room to help the people you love. Somewhere between seeing the possibility and participating in it, a familiar thought takes over.
That moment is a place to begin. There is a person bringing a lifetime of beliefs and feelings to every plan. That person deserves attention, too.
teachingTitle: Give your ambition a direction of its own.
teaching: Before we examine a belief, we need a desire worth examining it for. Let yourself want the visible things. Then stay long enough to understand what they hold for you: freedom, security, adventure, generosity, satisfaction, or a sense that you are participating in your own life.

The prosperity teachings behind IntentField ask you to attend to your inner life: the picture you hold of yourself, what you expect, what you repeatedly tell yourself, and the feeling you bring to receiving. They invite a relationship with abundance through desire, imagination, gratitude and openness. We carry that spiritual approach into ordinary decisions about work and money.

Begin with three lists. Write what would support your stability now. Write the possessions and experiences you desire. Then write the qualities and relationships you want to grow alongside your wealth. Keep all three. You can appreciate your life and want it to expand.

Choose one chief prosperity focus. Give it a sentence you can return to. Imagine an ordinary moment in the life it would make possible, including yourself and the feeling of living it. You may use pictures, words, or a sense of meaning.

Then choose a small action that lets your inner work meet experience. The larger desire can remain expansive while today's step is manageable. Your customer, circumstances and exact route remain open. You are practicing how you participate.

Maya begins by hearing the thought that appears before she sends her price. Jordan begins by choosing one service to explore. Each now has something specific to bring into the six-stage practice: Desire, Discover, Align, Rehearse, Build and Receive. These stages can repeat within a day.

example.name: Jordan's first direction
example.context: A fictional worked example. Jordan is 24, works shifts and is exploring video editing. These are intentions and planned actions, not customer results.
example.stability: Cover my regular bills and build a cash buffer.
example.experiences: Take a trip with my sister and eventually choose more of my working hours.
example.qualities: Become dependable, confident about asking questions, and more present with family.
example.focus: Build a video-editing service that earns through useful, well-delivered work.
example.meaning: I want more choice over my time and the satisfaction of building something of my own.
example.scene: I finish a project on Friday, receive a thank-you from a client and put my phone away for dinner. I feel capable and present.
example.action: Create a short sample with footage I have permission to use, then ask one local business owner what would make it useful.
example.review: Next Friday: review the response and what I learned about making the offer.

checklist: I have written all three lists without making my desire smaller for someone else.
I have chosen one chief focus and explained why it matters.
I have spent a moment with the feeling of a life I want to inhabit.
I have noticed a belief or hesitation to explore, without turning it into a verdict about myself.
I have chosen a small useful action and a time to review it.
I will record what happened and something I appreciate.
route: Meet the person behind the plan

Find an alignment you can live

Imagine the fulfilled life and rehearse today's response.

Review experience, appreciate what arrived, and choose next steps.
sourceNote: This original sample develops the V2.1 Wealth Primer. Its three-list vision and declarations draw on the supplied The Lazy Man's Way to Riches (physical PDF pages 26–32 and 39–43). Desire, feeling, gratitude, teachability and repeated application draw on the reviewed Your Wish Is Your Command material. The six-stage method, story, questions and examples are IntentField adaptations. Maya and Jordan are fictional teaching characters. This is a spiritual and educational practice; no particular income is promised.
